烫伤脱困（默认开）：扫帚模式 / 空袭 / 飞行跟随途中，女仆**真的**泡进岩:
Burn Escape (on by default): During broom mode / airstrike / flight follow, when the maid **actually** ends up in lava or catches fire, instantly (within the same tick) teleport her to the nearest air block — while riding a broom, 【move her and the broom together】 (same teleport code as "broom tow rope"; teleporting her alone would kick her off the broom).

【This is a separate layer from "Flight Hazard Avoidance"】That one is **predictive**: it steers her sideways before she enters / levels her out so she doesn't sink into the block; this one is **get out once she's already in** — knockback, terrain squeezing, or firework drift can all push her right into it, and prediction alone can't stop that.

【Why the flight side previously had no escape at all】The ground hazard block handling (Danger Escape) explicitly exempts "passengers": a maid in broom mode is **always** a passenger (she's riding the broom), and airstrike/flight follow spend all their time in the air — so none of these three modes had any escape.

【The check uses the vanilla one】isInLava / isOnFire — exactly "does vanilla want to burn her this tick" — same source as "Suffocation Escape uses isInWall". Being in water doesn't count (water puts out fire); not taking burn damage doesn't count (Fire Resistance potion / TLM fire protection trinket — those two already mean lava deals no damage).

【Teleport, not drift out】Lava deals 4 per second and she only has 20 HP — she can't wait for the broom's timed turn-based escape, so it teleports directly (clears fall damage / clears velocity). Landing spot = the nearest air block she fits in (both the standing block and the head block are air, and neither her own block nor the one below is a hazard block); if none is found in a full ring, it falls back to anywhere that can hold her (getting out of the fluid matters most). 1-second cooldown to prevent jitter. Search the log for "Burn Escape".

Off = no more life-saving teleport during flight (only predictive avoidance remains)
鞘翅外观（默认开）：需求：目前鞘翅的渲染只在空袭模式下会被渲染出来。而且渲染出来:
Elytra Appearance (default on): Requirement: Currently elytra rendering only happens in air-raid mode. And what gets rendered is always the vanilla elytra — can it use that elytra's own appearance? And render in all modes. Follow-up requirement: I want this rendering to be a general solution, not special-case adaptations. Avoid special-casing as much as possible. When enabled, both things are done together——

【① Render in all modes】As long as the maid's chestplate slot holds glidable equipment (vanilla elytra, or any mod glider that claims canElytraFly, including "gliding armor" like elytra chestplates), draw that pair of wings: while standing and mining / walking / following / idle, a pair of **folded** wings sits on her back; they only spread when flying (gliding) — exactly like vanilla players "wear an elytra, get wings on your back" (the old version only drew them during flight tasks or while gliding).

【② Use that elytra's own appearance · three-stage resolution】① First reflect the mod's **already-public** accessor — as long as this item has getType() and its returned object has a getTexture() returning a ResourceLocation (Icarus Wings works this way: getType().getTexture()/getTextureReversed()), or the item itself exposes getElytraTexture(...), just trust it, **without hardcoding any class names** (if that mod adds new wing items later, they render correctly with zero changes); ② If that fails, check MaidWingSkins' static table (only covers mods where "the texture is hidden in a private layer with no public accessor": the Mysterious Relics family); ③ If still unrecognized, fall back to vanilla textures/entity/elytra.png — it won't render wrong, just with the vanilla appearance.

【Why can't it "render correctly without knowing any mod at all"】Forge/NeoForge's IClientItemExtensions has no "tell me your elytra texture" hook at all (verified with javap; neither 1.20.1 nor 1.21.1 has it). Without a shared API, there's no universal solution. The three-stage approach is the most general form achievable: supported mods need zero adaptation; new mods either happen to match stage ①'s duck typing, or you add a resolution rule.

【Separate from "Self-Propelled Elytra"】Whether it can fly on its own is governed by the "Self-Propelled Elytra · Eligible Item List"; what it looks like is governed by this resolver — an ordinary elytra (feather-based) can also have its own appearance, it just won't self-propel.

Off = old behavior (only drawn during flight tasks/gliding, and always with the vanilla texture)

激流三叉戟·推进剂力度倍数（默认 1.0 = 不打折，范围 0.1~2.0）：用:
Riptide Trident · Propellant Force Multiplier (default 1.0 = no reduction, range 0.1~2.0): When using the Riptide trident as a 【propellant】 (takeoff / flight follow-up boost / airstrike altitude-recovery lift and dive dash), force = vanilla `3.0×(1+level)/4` × **1.3** (the tuning baseline) × this setting (by enchantment level: I 1.95 / II 2.93 / III 3.90 blocks/tick).

【Behavior mimics fireworks】The propellant is not a "one-shot impulse" — like a mounted firework, it **pulls the entire velocity vector** toward "look direction × current force" every tick (`v ← v×0.5 + look×(force/2)`, same form as vanilla mounted fireworks) — so **the vertical component is also handled by the propellant** (the old version only clamped horizontal; vertical was left alone, so takeoff would climb all the way up).

【Values taken from the in-water hit】Current force decays at **the player's in-water drag ×0.80/tick**, and stops once it falls to the normal gliding value (0.35 blocks/tick). Distance accumulates tick by tick via the recurrence: I ≈ 7.6 blocks / II ≈ 12.5 blocks / III ≈ 17.3 blocks (the closed form force ÷ (1 − 0.80) = 9.75 / 14.6 / 19.5 is the ideal upper bound). copying the player's hit (level III 12.9 blocks) and measured too slow — "Riptide III isn't even as fast as dive-flying on its own" — so the baseline is ×1.3.

【When to tune down / up】For more economy and stability, tune toward 0.1; to get back that feel, set it to 1÷1.3 ≈ 0.77; for more punch, tune toward 2.0. 0.1 is still one tenth of the vanilla force.

【Five maneuvers (named after modern air-combat tactics)】① Orbit (baseline, tied for first at 24% — radius/direction/speed still governed by the random-orbit system, and **direction randomly flips every 8 seconds**, see below); ② Weave (24%: circles while moving radially in and out ±22%, so the enemy can't predict which block she'll be on next); ③ Yo-yo (18%: altitude follows a slow wave, **turning slower up high and faster down low** — the real yo-yo trade of speed for altitude); ④ Extend (17%: periodically pulls out to the outermost ring then cuts back in, alternating "dealing damage" with "backing off for a breather", the most HP-efficient); ⑤ Figure-8 (17%: flips direction every 4 seconds, crisscrossing back and forth in front of the enemy).

【Switch every 20 seconds】Within the same encounter, re-roll every 20 seconds, and **guaranteed to differ from the previous one** — the old "one roll per encounter" meant, against a boss (the logged fight lasted 163 seconds), "one roll for two minutes", which is exactly why players said "every fight just keeps using Orbit".

【Orbit direction randomly flips every 8 seconds】Requirement: Don't keep going clockwise or counterclockwise the whole time… about an 8-second cycle. Randomly choose to keep going clockwise or counterclockwise. Every 8 seconds, a 50/50 chance decides "keep the same direction / flip it"; the flip only changes the sign of angular velocity, position stays continuous (not a teleport).

【The roll is deterministic】Derived from "maid UUID + which encounter this is for her": replaying the same save yields the same result, but her **next encounter will be a different one** (not the same one for life); multiple maids in the same encounter each roll independently, so you'll no longer see "a whole group circling the same ring".

【Two hard guarantees】① Altitude only increases, never decreases — the player's "base height above the enemy" setting holds under every maneuver (Yo-yo only goes higher); ② Radius and angular-velocity multipliers both stay within ±20%, and the final radius is still clamped by the caller to [min distance to enemy, max distance to enemy], so "random" can never turn into "drifting farther and farther away" or "right in their face".

Off = revert to old behavior (always Orbit; radius / direction / speed randomness still applies). Search the log for "Engagement Maneuvers" to see which one each maid rolled.

【Copies vanilla leash's own tiering】Vanilla leash physics has only three tiers (1.21.1 Leashable.tickLeash / 1.20.1 PathfinderMob.customServerAiStep, the literals are identical in both versions): distance > 10 blocks **lets go and drops the leash**, > 6 blocks applies an impulse toward the holder, 2~6 blocks **walks to 2 blocks from the holder**. This mod's rope "never breaks", so the first tier becomes "keep pulling" (if she goes too far, her own tether will teleport her—and the broom—back); the latter two tiers are what apply: > 6 blocks copies vanilla's 0.4·direction² impulse, 2~6 blocks uses "speed cap toward the owner" (= vanilla's followLeashSpeed semantics: walk until 2 blocks from you) instead of vanilla's pathfinding—vanilla recomputes an A* path every tick there, which is a server disaster once you have many maids; this mod only adds speed and leaves navigation alone.

【Scope】Only the **leashed tier** (she hasn't taken off yet and you're leading her along; Requirement: vanilla's leash logic is the player leading the maid along)—in that tier you are **not** her passenger and can move freely, so the rope can actually take force. The hanging tier (you're already dangling beneath her) is rigidly controlled by vanilla's riding positioning and doesn't take part in the tug.

【How to turn it off】Off = the rope is drawn but exerts no force (her own follow chain works as usual, just without that extra pull).

【It's literally the vanilla zombie-riding-chicken setup】Mounting goes through {@code startRiding(force)} (skipping vanilla's two gates), and driving goes through **the mount's own pathfinding** — vanilla {@code LivingEntity.aiStep} only runs travelRidden when "the first passenger is a player", and the {@code getControllingPassenger()} of horses/pigs/striders/camels **only recognizes players** too (verified in bytecode), so when a maid is the passenger they run **normal travel**, and navigation pushes them along as usual. This mod just feeds the destination (the owner's position) into its own {@code PathNavigation}; slopes/obstacle avoidance/jumping/vanilla animations are all handled by it — that's the "lazy downgrade".

【Rideable = capability detection, no hardcoded ids】Vanilla horses/donkeys/mules/skeleton horses/zombie horses, pigs, striders, and camels all implement {@code Saddleable} (verified by a full javap scan), and all require being **saddled**; modded mobs just need to implement this interface and be saddled — zero adaptation needed to ride.

【Speed】Requirement: take the max between the mount's max speed and the maid's max speed — converted into the multiplier fed to the mount's pathfinding ({@code max(mount, maid) / mount}, since the pathfinding speed parameter is a multiplier that gets multiplied by the mount's own movement speed attribute).

【She still fights while riding】TLM automatically switches the brain to RIDE_* when she's a passenger (the check is {@code isPassenger()}), and the maid's own chain is unaffected. Off = the baton no longer binds, and mounts act freely as in vanilla

【Why a single generic criterion won't work】Vanilla animals (horse/pig/camel) can be driven by this mod because vanilla handles "maid as passenger" through normal travel + pathfinding; but these two mod vehicle types **don't use vanilla's system at all**: Superb Warfare's rides aren't Saddleable and have no PathNavigation — they implement their own driving model with a processInput(short) bitmask + per-engine handling (ground/tracked/boat/helicopter/fixed-wing/airship); Ice and Fire dragons are neither Saddleable nor have saddles — riding is decided only by "tamed + owner + stage>2", and flight is driven by a separate IafDragonFlightManager.

【Attack】Superb Warfare's vehicle base class **already has built-in** "if a Mob passenger has a target, auto-aim and fire", so just have the maid sit in the weapon slot and give her the target herself; Ice and Fire dragons need breath to be explicitly triggered. See the next option for the toggle.

【How to ride】Exactly the same as vanilla animals: right-click the minion with the Riding Baton first, then right-click the maid (mount first, maid second). Once mounted, it uses the "her own movement logic" tier, and following/combat matches other land mounts.

【How this value works】It is a **hard floor**, coexisting with the soft correction above but with higher priority: whenever the height difference drops below this value, the circling pitch is **pinned straight to maximum nose-up** (regardless of the angle computed from the error), so she immediately enters a climb and will never keep sliding down; at the same time, the trigger threshold for "height-loss boost" is also raised to this value (below it counts as height loss, no need to wait until she drops out of the 10-block band), and the boost kicks in as soon as the cooldown is ready.

传送后客户端重建（默认开）：远距离传送后「女仆在服务端活着、客户端却看不见、也右:
Client rebuild after teleport (on by default): fixes the case where, after a long-distance teleport, the maid is alive on the server but invisible on the client and can't be right-clicked.

【Why she's invisible】A long-distance teleport makes the server send a teleport packet; on receiving it, the client interpolates her along tick by tick. If the first step (exactly 1/3 of the way between start and end) lands in a chunk the client hasn't loaded yet, the interpolation freezes on that block forever, the section she's in never compiles, and the render loop skips her entirely — model and hitbox both vanish (she can still fight mobs and bridge, you just can't see or click her). The server won't self-heal either: the position baseline is already aligned, delta≈0, so it thinks the client knows where she is.

【The fix】Intercept the teleport packet that would trigger interpolation and instead use "remove + spawn" to have the client rebuild the entity entirely (coordinates set in one go, no interpolation); also queue a follow-up packet delayed by 1 second to rebuild once more after the teleport actually takes effect, so the spawn packet carries the new coordinates beside her owner.

仿创造飞行（默认关，1.20.1 精简版）：让女仆悬浮并自由升降——创造模式飞行:
Creative-like Flight (off by default, 1.20.1 Lite): lets the maid hover and rise/descend freely — the feel of creative-mode flight.

【Why it's needed】Flight-granting items in modpacks come in all shapes and sizes (trinkets/armor sets/potion effects), and nearly all of them **only work on players** (hardcoded instanceof Player), so a maid wearing them won't budge an inch. This feature doesn't replicate each item's physics; instead: **if she qualifies (item table/effect table), this mod holds her up** — setNoGravity + applying velocity directly every tick, producing hovering and smooth movement.

【Two qualification paths (1.20.1 Lite)】①Item table (both hands/armor/inventory/trinket slots/extra containers) ②Effect table (potion effects naturally work on maids).

【Two paths cut in 1.20.1 vs 1.21.1】The gravity-zeroing heuristic (1.20.1 has no Attributes.GRAVITY attribute) and the two data-component paths @component/@component~text (data components are a 1.20.5+ mechanism).

【Deliberately not done】Doesn't recognize equipment with **built-in fuel** like Iron Jetpacks / diesel jetpacks: their thrust is bound to the player, so this mod's creative-like flight would bypass fuel out of thin air — that's cheating. Add them to the item table yourself if you want to use them.

【Safety】When the feature is turned off, if she's still in mid-air she'll soft-land first (stay gravity-free and descend slowly) before gravity is handed back, so she won't be dropped from high altitude.

鞘翅外观（默认开）：需求：目前鞘翅的渲染只在空袭模式下会被渲染出来。而且渲染出来:
Elytra Appearance (On by default): Requirement: Right now elytra rendering only happens in airstrike mode. And everything rendered is the vanilla elytra — can it use that elytra's own appearance? And render in all modes. Follow-up requirement: I want this rendering to be a general solution, not special-case adaptations. Avoid special-casing wherever possible. When enabled, do both at once——

【① Render in all modes】As long as the maid's chestplate slot holds glidable gear (vanilla elytra, or any mod glider that claims canElytraFly, including "gliding armor" like elytra chestplates), draw that pair of wings: standing mining / walking / following / idle, she has a pair of **folded** wings on her back; only when flying (gliding) do they spread — exactly like a vanilla player "wear an elytra, get wings on your back" (the old version only drew them during flight tasks or while actively gliding).

【② Use that elytra's own appearance · three-tier resolution】① First reflect the mod's **already-public** accessor — if the item has getType() and its returned object has a getTexture() returning a ResourceLocation (Icarus Wings works this way: getType().getTexture()/getTextureReversed()), or the item itself exposes getElytraTexture(...), trust it directly, **hardcoding no class names** (if that mod adds wing items later, zero changes needed to draw them right); ② if that fails, check MaidWingSkins' static table (only covers mods whose "textures are hidden in private layers with no public accessor": Enigmatic Legacy+); ③ if still unrecognized, fall back to vanilla textures/entity/elytra.png — it won't draw wrong, just vanilla-looking.

【Why it can't "draw correctly without knowing any mod at all"】NeoForge's IClientItemExtensions simply has no "tell me your elytra texture" hook (verified with javap); without a shared API there's no universal solution. The three-tier approach is the most general form achievable: supported mods need zero adaptation, and new mods either happen to match tier ①'s duck typing or you add a resolution rule.

【Separate from "self-propelled elytra"】Whether she can fly on her own is governed by the "self-propelled elytra · eligible item list"; what it looks like is governed by this resolver — a plain elytra (feather-type) can have its own appearance too, it just won't self-propel.

Off = old behavior (only drawn during flight tasks/gliding, and always the vanilla texture)
鞘翅外观·YSM 让位（默认开）：装了「是，史蒂夫模型」（YSM）且这只女仆用的:
Elytra Appearance · YSM Yield (default on): When "Yes Steve Model" (YSM) is installed and this maid uses a **YSM model**, this mod no longer draws its pair of wings **while she glides**, yielding to the YSM model's own pair.

【Why only the gliding case】Among YSM's built-in models, only two have wings tied to the elytra: `21_saint` hooks the wing bone's visibility to `ysm.has_elytra` (which only recognizes the vanilla elytra) and only spreads them when gliding; `09_hailuo`'s `Elytra` bone is normally hidden with `scale:0`. In other words, **YSM models have no wings on their back while standing/walking** — that case is still drawn by this mod (otherwise YSM models would have no wings while standing), and only during gliding do both sides have wings and overlap. This option yields at that moment.

【How to use】Take the "Patrol Chart" (paper + compass + ink sac): **right-click** to open the UI → click "＋ Create a route" → on its management page, bind the maid and click "Start marking" → after leaving the UI, **middle-click** (no sneaking needed; works in the air or on the ground) to record a marker at your position → then **right-click** back into the UI and click "Connect" to join the ends into a closed loop. **Connecting has no requirements at all** (since v1.3.9.3: the old criteria — point count / slope / self-intersection / radius / blocking blocks — are now only ⚠ warnings; you can still connect even if you break them, and the consequences are on you). 【What about enemies】When enemies are around she **still engages them first** (climb → circle/bomb), and returns to the route on her own once they're gone — this comes free from the phase order, no extra configuration needed.

【Why it's tied to home】Requirement: Since it's patrol, it effectively replaces the original home mode. So this feature only applies to maids in broom mode under home mode. Turning this off = bound routes stop working, and broom mode goes back to the original home-guarding circling.

【What happens if you delete a route】Deleting a route = **the maids bound to it are invalidated too and return to their default state** (back to the original home-guarding circling / follow / hover), so you don't have to unbind them one by one; it doesn't matter if she isn't present right now (chunk not loaded) — she'll be invalidated the same way the next time she's loaded (the invalidation is **persisted**: deleting a route records an id server-wide, see PatrolRevocation).

【Troubleshooting】Search the log for "broom patrol"; use the command /maid_smart broom_patrol status to see whether it's in effect.
新建航迹的默认净空半径（格，默认 1.5，0.5~6.0）：航迹每个采样点周围要:

It's also the source of the threshold for the "two route segments too close" reminder (warns if they're closer than 2× this value).

Each trail stores its own copy (the value at marking time); changing this setting only affects trails **created afterward**. Larger = starts ascending earlier (wider aerial corridor), smaller = hugs obstacles more closely.

【Why still check obstacles】Requirement: (But there needs to be a precondition: no blocking blocks.) — it checks the dense sample points **on the curve**, not just the markers: both markers themselves may be in air, yet the path between them can easily cut through a mountain. Finding one only gives a hint, not a gate (Requirement: Don't make it a gate — leave it to the maid's own pathfinding).

【Five maneuvers (named after modern air-combat tactics)】① Orbit (baseline, tied for first at 24% — radius/direction/speed still handled by the random-orbit system, and **the direction randomly flips every 8 seconds**, see below); ② Weave (24%: circles while moving radially in and out ±22%, so the enemy can't tell how many blocks out she'll be next beat); ③ Yo-yo (18%: altitude slowly oscillates, **slower turns up high, faster down low** — the real yo-yo trade of speed for altitude); ④ Extend (17%: periodically pulls out to the outermost ring then cuts back in, alternating "dealing damage" with "backing off for a breather", the most health-efficient); ⑤ Figure-8 (17%: flips direction every 4 seconds, crossing back and forth in front of the enemy).

【New maneuver every 20 seconds】Within the same encounter it re-rolls every 20 seconds, and **is guaranteed to differ from the previous one** — the old "one roll per encounter" meant, against a boss (the fight in the test logs lasted 163 seconds), "one roll for two minutes", which is exactly why players said "after so many fights it's always orbit".

【Orbit direction flips randomly every 8 seconds】Requirement: Don't keep going clockwise or counter-clockwise the whole time… about an 8-second cycle. Randomly pick whether to keep going clockwise or counter-clockwise. Every 8 seconds a 50/50 roll decides "keep the same direction / flip"; flipping only changes the sign of angular velocity, position stays continuous (no teleporting).

【The roll is deterministic】Derived from "maid UUID + which encounter this is for her": replaying the same save gives the same result, while her **next encounter will be different**; multiple maids in the same fight each roll their own, so you'll no longer see "a whole group circling the same ring".

【Two hard guarantees】① Altitude is only added, never subtracted — the player's "how many blocks above the enemy" baseline holds under every maneuver; ② radius and angular-velocity multipliers stay within ±20%, and the final radius is still clamped to [min distance to enemy, max distance to enemy], so "random" can never become "drifting farther and farther away" or "right in their face".

Off = reverts to old behavior (always orbit). Search the log for "Engagement Maneuvers
高悠悠高度幅度（格，默认 4，0~16）：「高悠悠」这一种机动在**你设的基础盘:

【It will never push her below the baseline altitude】The amplitude is **added** to the base altitude (a slow wave from 0 to amplitude), so the "how many blocks above the enemy the base sits" spec doesn't move a single byte. 空袭·空中防叠罗汉（默认开）：多只女仆同时接同一个敌人时，鞘翅空袭（近战 / 远:

武装拴绳总开关（默认开）：手持武装拴绳右击【飞行中的】女仆，把自己挂到她下方（像:
Armed Leash master switch (default on): hold the Armed Leash and right-click a 【flying】 maid to hang yourself below her (like the gunner in an attack helicopter's gunner seat; **right-clicking her while on a broom = switch to the gunner seat**, right-clicking while bound = sit back in the broom's pilot seat) — she flies as usual and fires ranged weapons as usual, and so do you; right-click again (or press sneak-jump) to release. **No longer auto-releases on the ground** ("the rope won't snap on its own"); **she doesn't set your height or your seat** (while leashed she just hovers in place and doesn't write a single height value, engaging enemies as usual; when she's standing on the ground she instead spreads out horizontally to stand side by side, no longer overlapping your model); only falling into water for more than 0.6 seconds will drop you (drowning is fatal); on release, if you're in the air you get 5 seconds of fall damage immunity; while hanging, wall-clip/crush damage is fully negated.

【v1.3.9.4: can also leash to ridden vehicles】Requirement: The Armed Leash could be expanded. It could also leash to ridden vehicles. When she's currently riding a helicopter / dragon / ground mount or other vehicle: ① you can leash on the same way (right-clicking her directly, or right-clicking the vehicle she's riding, both work); ② the hanging **anchor is that vehicle** (hanging below the helicopter is the gunner seat; hanging below her while she sits in the cabin would get you pinched by the hull); ③ **it doesn't take the vehicle's driver seat** — the player is still a passenger of "her", and how the vehicle flies or who's driving isn't changed by a single byte; ④ if the player was already sitting on that vehicle, grabbing the rope first dismounts you, then hangs you below her (the reverse of the "sit back on the broom" tier).

Slot 2 Mace Smash (on by default, **1.21.1 only**: the mace only exists in 1.21, so 1.20.1 has no such entry).

Requirement: I was just running the game and had the maid do a melee air strike, and I was holding a mace too. So can I trigger the mace's damage bonus and other effects normally? I'd rather the player get these effects, without being affected by the sitting state.

【Why you couldn't get it before】The mace's fall bonus reads entirely from the single field fallDistance (MaceItem.canSmashAttack = fallDistance > 1.5 && !isFallFlying(), and damage is then computed in three tiers: 4f / 12+2(f-3) / 22+(f-8)), and that field is only accumulated in Entity.move → Entity.checkFallDamage — **passengers don't run move** (rideTick zeroes velocity first, then the vehicle's positionRider calls setPos directly, which is also how this mod's hanging positioning works), so dangling below her, your fallDistance is always 0 and you can't land a single smash.

【Only the air-strike tier applies】Requirement: By mace I mean when the maid is doing a melee air strike and carrying the player at the same time, and the player smashes with a mace right then... open the backdoor here, but don't open broom mode. So **when a melee air strike carries you down in a dive, it still counts as falling**, while **the broom tier records nothing at all** — the broom is transport, not a dive; gliding level on a broom and slowly dropping two or three blocks shouldn't earn a smash (after the threshold was lowered earlier, the broom's slow descent could build it up too; this batch rolls that back per the player's request). The broom tier also won't print the "Mace Door Player=" line.

【How it's calculated now】Since it's her that's moving, this mod keeps a copy for you based on **your actual descent**: however many blocks she drops in that dive, your smash counts for that many blocks (the vanilla sound effects, nearby knockback and damage bonus all run through on their own). One descent buys only one smash (consumed on use, cleared immediately, same as vanilla's resetFallDistance after a successful smash); hovering/slow descent doesn't count (if a single 2-tick sample drops less than 0.2 blocks = 0.1 blocks/tick, the accumulator is clamped back to 1.0, so drifting while hovering can't build up an over-smash either); her landing = cleared.

Off = fully reverts to vanilla (no smash while hanging).

Vanilla mob riding master switch (on by default): hold the **Riding Baton** and right-click a **saddled** mount to bind it, then right-click your maid (or the other way around, order doesn't matter) → she climbs on, and from then on **follows her owner** (stops once she's 5 blocks away). 【It's literally the vanilla zombie-riding-chicken setup】Mounting goes through startRiding(force) (skipping vanilla's two gates), and driving uses **the mount's own pathfinding** — vanilla LivingEntity.aiStep only runs travelRidden when "the first passenger is a player", and horse/pig/strider/camel getControllingPassenger() also **only recognizes players** (verified in bytecode), so when a maid is the passenger they run **normal travel**, and navigation keeps pushing them along as usual. This mod just feeds the destination (the owner's position / where she was already headed) into its own PathNavigation, and slopes/obstacle avoidance/jumping/vanilla animations are all handled by it — that's the "lazy downgrade" trick.

【Rideable = capability detection, no hardcoded IDs】Vanilla horse/donkey/mule/skeleton horse/zombie horse, pig, strider, and camel all implement Saddleable (verified by a full javap scan), and all require **being saddled**; modded mobs just need to implement this interface and be saddled — zero adaptation needed to ride.

【Speed】Requirement: take the max between the mount's max speed and the maid's max speed — converted into the multiplier fed to the mount's pathfinding (max(mount, maid) / mount, since the pathfinding speed parameter is a multiplier that gets multiplied by the mount's own movement speed attribute).

【She fights as usual while riding】When she's a passenger, TLM automatically switches her brain to RIDE_* (criterion: isPassenger()), and the maid's own chain is unaffected. Off = the baton no longer binds, and mounts act freely as in vanilla.

传送后客户端重建（默认开·issue #36）：治「远距离传送后女仆在服务端活着:
Client rebuild after teleport (on by default · issue #36): fixes "after a long-distance teleport the maid is alive server-side but invisible client-side".

【Root cause】A large jump makes the client interpolate per tick via Entity.lerpTo(target, 3 steps); the first step lands exactly at 1/3 between start and end. If that landing point is in a chunk the client 【hasn't loaded】, the entity drops out of the tick list, interpolation freezes permanently at 1/3, and her section is never compiled → model and hitbox both vanish. Server-side, since the position baseline is already aligned and delta≈0, it never sends position packets again (no self-healing). This explains "she can fight mobs and place blocks, but you can't see her or right-click her".

【Fix】① When ServerEntity.sendChanges detects a large position baseline jump (>64 blocks), intercept the teleport packet and use "remove + spawn" instead so the client fully rebuilds (coordinates set in one go, no interpolation at all); ② fire a second shot 1 second later — by then the teleport has actually taken effect, so the spawn packet carries the new coordinates near the player (that chunk is loaded client-side).

Off = back to vanilla behavior (she may be invisible after a long-distance teleport; requires /maid_smart resync or reloading the save).

Creative-like flight (off by default): lets the maid hover and rise/descend freely — the feel of creative-mode flight.

【Why it's needed】In modpacks, flight-granting items are wildly varied (trinkets/armor sets/potion effects/zero-gravity spells), and nearly all of them **only work on players** (hardcoded instanceof Player) — the maid wearing them won't budge an inch. This feature doesn't replicate each item's physics; instead: **if she qualifies (item list / effect list / zero gravity), this mod holds her up** — setNoGravity + directly applying velocity every tick, producing hovering and smooth movement.

【Three qualification paths】① Item list (both hands / armor / backpack / trinket slots / extra containers) ② Effect list (potion effects work on maids naturally) ③ Gravity attribute ≈ 0 (generic heuristic, covers every zero-gravity source, no need to name mods).

【Deliberately not done】Doesn't recognize equipment with **built-in fuel** like Iron Jetpacks / diesel jetpacks: their thrust is tied to the player, so this mod's creative-like flight would bypass fuel out of thin air — that's cheating. If you want to use them, add them to the item list yourself.

干活时移速压回 0 好感档: Cap movement speed to the 0-affection baseline while working
默认开：工作/生产任务的女仆不论好感多高，移动速度都按「0 好感档」走（钳到基础: Default on: working/production maids move at '0-favor' speed regardless of favor (clamped to base 0.7); combat / idle / follow / riding keep their own. Note TLM has no favor-speed bonus - visible speed comes from curio slots and the stroll multiplier.
干活时移速压回 0 好感档（默认开）：工作/生产任务的女仆，不论好感度多高，移动:
Cap movement speed to the 0-affection baseline while working (default on): a maid on a work/production task moves at the "0-affection baseline" speed no matter how high her favorability; combat tasks / idle / follow / riding keep their normal speed (Requirement: combat tasks and idle keep the level-3 bonus).

[Correcting a premise first] TLM 1.5.3 actually has NO "higher favorability = faster movement" bonus — the official jar, the pack's [Guochuang] fork jar and the server jar were all scanned class-by-class: FavorabilityManager writes only attack/health into attributes (the favorability level table has no SPEED entry at all), and TLM's own in-game book says only "Higher favorability will increase the maid's health and attack".

[So where does "high favorability = darting around" come from] It is INDIRECT: (1) the favorability level decides the bauble slot count (level 0-1 = 10 slots / level 2 = 20 / level 3 = 30), so a high-affection maid can equip more movement/accelerating baubles; (2) this mod's "Walk Speed Multiplier" (Movement & Behaviour) multiplies her base 0.7, and a server config still on the old default 0.7 measures about 8 blocks/s (faster than a sprinting player's 5.61); (3) this mod also deliberately removed the vanilla walking brake window, so the speed looks "never stopping".

[What this option does] While working it clamps the maid's EFFECTIVE movement speed to her base value (0.7 = the bare 0-affection, no-bauble value). The technique copies this mod's "Ride Baton" mount-speed transfer: every tick it installs a self-correcting additive modifier so the effective value stays equal to the base — no saved attribute is written, it is idempotent, and any other source (baubles/potions) is auto-compensated; switching back to combat/idle removes the modifier and her real speed returns immediately.

[When it does not interfere] Sitting / passenger / riding (she does not use her own legs then); combat tasks (including third-party IAttackTask); idle / follow. Off = no modifier is installed at all, byte-identical to the old version.
干活时不许出圈（默认开）：需求：女仆工作的时候喜欢乱窜——不停地在多个地方以极高:
Keep work-wander inside the circle (default on): player feedback — "when she works she keeps darting around: constantly moving between many places at very high speed as if hunting for a task target; it looks bad, and she easily runs out of the circle I drew with the compass".

[Why she wanders outside the circle] Cooking/brewing/slaughter enter a "wander while waiting" branch when there is nothing to do (no furnace / no stand / no animal): every 2 seconds they pick a random spot 8 blocks away and walk to it, looking for work on the way. Picking that spot does pass through the "work circle" (no leaving it in home mode) — but in FOLLOW mode (non-home) the circle effectively does not exist: the old code always allowed it, so she changes to a random direction every 2 seconds and darts all over the map looking for work.

[What this option does] In follow mode the wander also gets a circle: centred on YOUR position (following means staying near you), radius = "Schedule Activity Radius" (that setting, default 12 blocks; smaller = she stays more honestly nearby), and the spot must fall inside it. The anchor also changes from "her current position" to this fixed centre — otherwise "every 2 seconds randomly shift 8 blocks around herself" is a random walk with no restoring force, drifting dozens of blocks in a few dozen steps (exactly the "darting" mechanism). Home mode still uses the circle you drew (compass/work marker).

[What is unaffected] Combat / follow / idle / building (building stands still and places from a blueprint, it does not wander). Off = follow mode is completely unbounded (byte-identical to the old version).
罗盘圈优先（默认开）：让排班表的 home 也读取之前用罗盘画出来的圈，并且罗盘:
Player-drawn circle takes priority (default on): let the schedule book's home also read the circle the player drew earlier with the compass, and the compass has higher priority — a maid working is not allowed to leave the circle; resting and sleeping also follow the in-circle rules.

[Who draws the circle] The Kappa Compass (right-click a block to record the work/idle/sleep points, then right-click the maid to write them) writes the same TLM schedule anchor; the schedule book / build behaviour, when no anchors are configured, take HER CURRENT SPOT as the anchor (auto-anchor home). Of the two sources, only the compass is drawn by the player by hand.

[What this option does] It records a flag for "the player drew a circle" (set when the compass writes anchors). After that: (1) the schedule book's auto-anchoring no longer overwrites it with her current position; (2) build behaviour no longer displaces it with "current coordinates"; (3) turning the schedule off (or any other path) no longer zeroes the circle. In one sentence — a circle the player drew is not touched by anyone except the player drawing it again (or changing it in the TLM GUI).

[What is unaffected] Off = auto-anchoring may again overwrite a player-drawn circle.
默认开：烧制/酿造/宰杀没活可干时的闲逛，取点锚点改为固定圆心（home = 玩: Default on: idle wandering for cooking / brewing / butchering picks points around a fixed centre (home circle or the owner) and follow mode must stay inside it. Radius = schedule activity range; off = follow mode unlimited.
默认开：玩家用河童的罗盘画的圈会记一个「玩家圈」标记——排班表与建造的自动锚定一: Default on: circles drawn with the kappa compass get a 'player circle' mark - schedule and build auto-anchoring yields, so your circle is never overwritten; even in follow mode work points stay inside it. Off = old behavior.
非战斗模式下移速硬上限（默认开）：需求：本模组在非战斗模式下，女仆的速度不能比玩:
Non-combat walk speed cap (default on): player's words - "in non-combat mode the maid's speed must not exceed the player's. Even when she is hunting for a task target. By default it may at most match the player's sprint speed. I want to see what this mod did to the maid's task seeking - that may be the culprit behind all the darting around."

[Which speed path does "hunting for a task target" actually take - verified layer by layer with javap] (1) The brain writes WALK_TARGET (or a task calls PathNavigation.moveTo directly) -> vanilla MoveToTargetSink turns it into a Path; (2) PathNavigation feeds the next path node to MoveControl.setWantedPosition(x,y,z,speedModifier) every tick; (3) TLM's MaidMoveControl.tick computes "speed = speedModifier x getAttributeValue(MOVEMENT_SPEED)" in the MOVE_TO / STRAFE branch and then calls Mob.setSpeed; (4) Mob.setSpeed has only two lines - LivingEntity.setSpeed(value) (writes the speed field) + setZza(value) (writes the forward input zza), and travel uses exactly these two values to compute this tick's displacement.

[The conclusion is hard] Every speed at which the maid walks on her own legs must pass through the single gate Mob.setSpeed - navigation walking, direct moveTo, idle WALK_TARGET, farm work, following, mining travel: none can avoid it. (The only two that do not pass through it are the direct setDeltaMovement velocity-vector writes: one push step when bridging, self-preservation fleeing, flight/broom - those are not "walking" and this switch does not touch them.)

[Why the default equals the player's sprint speed] A table was measured on this mod's dedicated server (maid MOVEMENT_SPEED = 0.7, her bare value); writing speedModifier as the multiplier, the measured cruise speed in blocks/sec is: 0.3 -> 1.9 | 0.4 -> 3.3 (default stroll) | 0.5 -> 4.9 | 0.6 -> 6.0 | 0.7 -> 8.2 | 1.0 -> 14 (player walking 4.32, sprinting 5.61; about +-20% variation across terrain/machines at the same setting). In other words the multipliers TLM gives the maid by default (1.0 for following/attack positioning, 0.6x1.5 = 0.9 for this mod's mining travel) all measure 8-14 blocks/sec - already faster than the player's sprint. That is exactly the number behind "moving around at extremely high speed". Interpolating that table: 0.5 -> 4.9 and 0.6 -> 6.0, and the player sprints at 5.61, which falls between them -> about a 0.56 multiplier. That is where the default cap "5.61 blocks/sec = the player's sprint" comes from (0.4 only reaches 3.3, slower than the player's 4.32 walking speed, so the cap cannot be 0.4 - that is the "stroll" setting, not the cap).

[What this switch does] In non-combat, the value handed to Mob.setSpeed is hard-clamped to no more than the "cap" item (default 0.56, same unit as the "stroll speed multiplier" / "mining move speed"; it only clamps downward, never raises). This is an absolute cap - even if baubles double her MOVEMENT_SPEED, what is clamped is "the number finally handed in", so she still cannot be faster than the player.

[When it does NOT clamp] Combat (attack tasks including third-party IAttackTask / in combat / solo tactics in control - the player said "in non-combat mode", and in combat she must move to dodge, so no clamping); self-preservation fleeing (low health / fleeing / escaping danger - clamping there is suicide); flight / broom airborne (she is not on her legs then); sitting / passenger / sleeping; ownerless maids (the same rule as follow tightening / move suppression).

[Turning it off] Mob.setSpeed is never touched, byte-for-byte identical to the old build (this mod's own 1.5x mining travel, woodcutting, slaughter chasing all come back as they were).
非战斗移速上限（默认 0.56，范围 0.05~1.5）：与「散步速度倍率」「挖:
Non-combat walk speed cap value (default 0.56, range 0.05~1.5): the same unit as the "stroll speed multiplier" and "mining move speed" (a multiplier on her bare 0.7 movement speed).

[Why 0.56 by default] The comparison table: 0.3 -> 1.9, 0.4 -> 3.3, 0.5 -> 4.9, 0.6 -> 6.0, 0.7 -> 8.2, 1.0 -> 14 (blocks/sec). The player walks at 4.32 and sprints at 5.61 - interpolating to "equal to the player's sprint" gives about 0.56, hence the default.

[How to tune] Larger (e.g. 0.6~1.0) loosens it back toward the old sprinting; smaller (e.g. 0.3) makes her more docile and slow at work. Note that below 0.2 she barely moves in practice (she stutters step by step). This item only takes effect while the "non-combat walk speed cap" switch is on.

§eTakeoff speed for fixed-wings§r: the engine's lift term is §e「lift ∝ current speed」§r, while gravity is about 0.06 per tick — with the AC-130H's parameters, §eat speed 0.30 lift is only 0.01/tick, and at 0.70 only 0.02/tick§r, both far below 0.06, so pitching up before she is fast enough means dropping right after liftoff. Therefore: §etakeoff threshold 1.20§r (the roll keeps full thrust 3.0, sprint slot engaged), §eloiter / climb gears get throttle floors (1.8 / 3.0)§r, and §ethe speed cap uses the fixed-wing's own 2.60§r. That log entry also shows §e「thrust=」§r, and the roll log shows §e「horizontal speed=x/1.20」§r.
§eFixed-wing cruise mode§r: she §eruns four loops herself§r — heading goes through the mouse channel, the roll angle is written straight to full (45°) when turning, thrust only keeps her 「not stalling and not dragging her feet」, and §ealtitude directly drives vertical speed§r (not using pitch to chase altitude, which inevitably overshoots). Turning is aerodynamically limited: the rudder authority cap is only §e「0.3 + 3.2 × |roll|/90」§r, combined with AC-130H's yaw coefficient 0.9 ⇒ §emax angular velocity 1.71°/tick§r, so §eturn radius ≈ speed ÷ 0.0298§r — to shrink the radius, lower the speed and write the roll angle to full. The carrot only gives her §eone point§r: no enemy = §eabove the owner§r (dash over, make a wide turn, come back = circling the owner); enemy present = §edirectly above the enemy§r (repeatedly dive past overhead and turn around = shuttle bombing, with bombs dropped as usual by the bombing chain on each pass). §eThe 「give up on the enemy if the owner is too far」 gate is relaxed to 200 blocks§r for fixed-wing (a single pass + turnaround naturally takes her 100–200 blocks out). §eRadius§r: §ecruise speed 0.80 (radius ≈27 blocks)§r, §ethe roll angle is written straight to 45° when turning§r (no longer waiting for the left/right inputs to slowly roll), and §emouse channel 12§r (only at 0.80 speed can she get full rudder authority). §eAltitude§r: the carrot's altitude only relates to the owner/enemy, not to the hills underfoot, so as soon as a hill rises she slams right into it; and crash damage is §e18 × (speed − 0.2)²§r (about 6.5 points per hit at 0.80 speed). So she adds a §e「terrain clearance line」§r: target altitude = §emax(carrot altitude, highest ground underfoot and along the look-ahead path + 14 blocks)§r, with look-ahead distance converted from current speed (about 80 blocks), scanning three columns each along the travel direction and the target direction; when pushed up by terrain, the climb rate is relaxed to §e0.30 blocks/tick§r. 主动切换战斗（默认开）：你被有来源的攻击打（怪物/玩家/弹射物；摔落、岩浆等环境: Auto-engage (on by default): when you take damage from a sourced attack (mob/player/projectile; fall or lava damage does not count, so accidents do not call her in) or you attack a hostile mob, nearby maids (16 blocks by default) drop whatever they are doing — mining/woodcutting/smelting/building/following — and switch to combat to protect you. Attacking passive animals such as cows or sheep does not start a fight, so butchering does not draw every maid's blade; neutral mobs already hostile to you (an angry wolf/bee/polar bear, etc.) count as combatants: when they attack they trigger the engagement and are treated as threats when deciding when to restore, while calm ones still do not count; if a maid is attacked by a mob, she and her nearby sisters engage immediately. Which combat mode: every attack task is asked whether she can actually obtain a weapon it accepts — the scan covers the main hand + backpack (including the compression box's extension slots) + extra containers (Sophisticated Backpacks, Traveler's Backpack); offhand and trinket slots do not count (those items are never auto-equipped to the main hand, so counting them would only switch her into a mode where she cannot deal damage). Spell tasks use a separate rule: she must actually carry spell books/catalysts (main hand/offhand/backpack/trinket slots, or the spell addon's own data already lists her spell books — Irons' Spellbooks, Ars Nouveau, Psi, Goety, Useful Magic, Mana and Artifice, Wizardry, Youkai's Homecoming and SlashBlade providers all count; SlashBlade and Youkai's Homecoming are ignored by default because they are weapons with their own dedicated modes). When the pool contains mod-specific tasks, the five vanilla tasks step aside entirely ("Mod task priority" is on by default; turn it off for pure weighted randomness); the "third-party mode blacklist" only excludes the Puppeteer — SlashBlade mode / Battle mode can still be switched into, after which this mod steps aside; gun mode additionally requires a gun in her backpack plus matching ammo (Qiandao energy guns need no ammo); the two air-raid tasks (air melee/air ranged) are manual-only and never enter the pool. If nothing matches — she has no attack item at all — she does not engage and keeps her current task; the "skip when unarmed" switch restores the old bare-handed fallback. Far enemies (>5 blocks) pick ranged; at close range (≤5 blocks) with both available, the melee:ranged preference weight decides (default 3:1 favoring melee; adjustable in the "Auto-engage" section; 0 means never pick/switch to that type).
战中动态换战术：开战后每秒评估一次——她用远程时敌人近身（≤5 格）且拿得到近战: In-fight tactic switching: once combat starts she re-evaluates every second — if she is using ranged and an enemy closes in (≤5 blocks) and she can obtain a melee weapon (main hand / backpack, including the compression box, Sophisticated Backpacks and Traveler's Backpack; includes Epic Fight/SlashBlade and other mod melee weapons) she switches to melee immediately; if she is using melee and the enemy is too far even to jump to (>6 blocks) but still within targeting range (≤16 blocks) she switches to ranged kiting. The 5~6 block hysteresis band prevents flip-flopping; melee/ranged swapping also applies to mod tasks: mod tasks can be switched into and out of (the Puppeteer never participates; SlashBlade mode / Battle mode can be switched into, but once inside she is not switched out for the rest of this fight — this mod steps aside and she finishes with that mod's gameplay), still judged by distance — to keep a mode out of auto-switching entirely, write it as "do not participate" in the mode table above. The two air-raid tasks are manual-only and are not retuned mid-fight (doing so would break the firework/glide/wing-fold-slam chain); while riding a Qiandao vehicle she is not retuned either — the task is whatever you selected by hand. Restoring still returns her to the pre-combat task, unaffected by mid-fight weapon swaps. Restoring also brings back "guard/follow" and her schedule state: if no snapshot was recorded her settings are left completely untouched, and after restoring the run log prints "pre-combat mode restored: guard (home)=on/follow" for verification; anti-jitter: tactic changes have a minimum hold and a reverse cooldown (after a flip-flop is detected she keeps the current tactic for a while), all tunable in the "Auto-engage" section. Restore grace: after combat the schedule waits a few seconds before taking over (to avoid threat-flicker tugging), duration tunable in the "Shift Schedule" section. About 10 seconds after threats disappear she automatically returns to the original task (a miner keeps mining; delay tunable in the "Auto-engage" section). A task you changed by hand during combat is never flipped back by auto-restore — if the system sees the task was changed it simply exits and leaves her alone; "threats gone" uses a separate small threat radius (8 blocks by default, so distant mobs do not keep her from returning to work);
宠物/友方单位免伤（默认开，开关在「战斗与自保 → 玩家伤害策略」页的「玩家宠物: Pet/friendly-unit immunity (on by default; switch under Combat & Self-Preservation → Player Damage Policy, "Player pets / friendly units immunity"): she will not attack, and will not hit with splash/AoE/gunfire/explosions, any of these — (1) mobs whose name contains "player pet" or "owner's pet" or starts with "MaidNoAttack": any of display name/custom name/plain name counts, renaming with a name tag or anvil takes effect immediately, and an already-locked grudge is cleared within 2 seconds; (2) tamable pets / mod summons / other players' maids that have a player owner (OwnableEntity with a non-empty owner UUID, still recognized when the owner is offline) — units owned by her own owner or a same-team teammate are always immune, with PvP off any player-owned unit is immune, and only with PvP on and different teams do they remain fightable as in vanilla; (3) damage attribution follows the projectile's owner, so gun bullets, arrows and spell projectiles hitting a pet are blocked the same way (damage not caused by a maid is untouched, so players/mobs can still hit pets). Turning the whole guard off restores vanilla behavior and she will attack pets again.
